mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, exceeding a 2% month-over-month decline, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle with input disruptions and rising costs.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of instances following a triggered INDPRO decline, indicating the market is shrugging off the supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, increasing by more than 0.5 percentage points over a 3-month period, signals a weakening labor market and slowing consumer demand that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and retail sales remain strong during periods of rising unemployment, indicating the labor market weakness is not translating to consumer demand.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that will slow economic growth and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Equity market volatility, as measured by the VIX, fails to rise significantly (t-test p > 0.1) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, indicating the restrictive policy is not creating market stress.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts decline by more than 10% year-over-year, it signals a weakening housing market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Homebuilder stocks outperform the broader market during periods of declining housing starts, indicating the housing weakness is not broadly impacting consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI inflation rate exceeds 3% year-over-year, it signals rising price pressures that will erode consumer purchasing power and negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Real consumer spending remains strong (rising > 2% YoY) during periods of elevated inflation, indicating the price pressures are not significantly impacting consumer behavior.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment growth slows to less than 100,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims fail to rise significantly (t-test p > 0.1) during periods of slowing payroll growth, indicating the labor market weakness is not leading to increased layoffs.

mechanism_narrative: When real consumer spending (RSAFS) declines month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals a consumer-led recession that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines MoM for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Consumer confidence rises and retail inventories fall during periods of declining consumer spending, indicating the spending weakness is not broadly impacting the consumer sector.
